News.title: Child left seriously injured and rushed to hospital after being struck by car in city centre
News.content:
HORROR CRASH Child left seriously injured and rushed to hospital after being struck by car in city centre

A CHILD has been rushed to hospital after being struck by a car in a city centre.

Emergency services were called to Huddersfield Road in Manchester on Saturday following reports of a vehicle collision involving a child.





The victim has been taken to hospital for treatment of their serious injuries.

Greater Manchester Police were alerted to the incident at around 12.35pm on May 23.

At the scene of the horror crash in Oldham, a large police cordon was put in place.

The driver of the car remained at the scene to assist officers.



The force has said that it has not made any arrests yet and is continuing with its investigation into the matter.

The cordon stretching from Asda on Hudderfield Road to Cypress Road has since been lifted.

News.title: Trump vows Strait of Hormuz will reopen as Iran peace deal is being finalised in major breakthrough
News.content:
DONALD Trump has announced that a deal between the US and Iran has been “largely negotiated.”

Details will be announced “shortly” – but the US President confirmed that the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened – after the Islamic Republic and the mediator, Pakistan, submitted a new proposal to end the war in the 11th hour.





In a bombshell post on TruthSocial, he said: “An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalisation between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed.

“Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly.

“In addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened.”

Leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Bahrain, as well as ministers of Pakistan, have been pushing to hammer out a final deal.

The post comes after what the US president describes as a “very good call” with leaders from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Jordan and Bahrain.

Trump had a separate call with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he said also went “very well”.

He hailed the deal as a “Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE.”

Major points of contention remain murky – for one, whether Iran will still manage the shipping lane.



Trump also did not mention whether the warring nations had reached an agreement on Iran’s nuclear weapons or the highly enriched uranium.

An official, speaking anonymously, said that Iran and the US had finally made “significant progress” towards a deal but warned that “last-minute disputes” could blow up the efforts.

He said the potential deal would include an official declaration of the war’s end, with two-month negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.



Meanwhile, Iran had signalled “narrowing differences” in negotiations with the US after Pakistan’s army chief held more talks in Tehran.

Iran’s Fars news ‌agency reported that the theocratic regime would remain under its own management according ⁠to ​the ⁠latest exchanged ⁠text of the deal.

It also dismissed Trump’s announcement of reopening the strait as part ‌of ​a “largely ‌negotiated” deal ⁠as “incomplete ⁠and inconsistent ‌with ​reality.”

“Based on the latest exchanged text, if a possible agreement is reached, the Strait of Hormuz will still be under Iran’s management,” the report from Fars said.

“Although Iran has agreed to allow the number of passing ships to return to the level before the war, this does not at all mean ‘free passage’ to the pre-war situation.



“The management of the strait, determining the route, time, manner of passage, and issuing permits, will remain exclusively under the control and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

This is not the first time in recent weeks that a deal has been described as close.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told journalists in India that “there’s been some progress made” and “there may be news later today.”

News.title: I wrote the book on Murdaugh trial with clerk who brought down Alex’s conviction – warning signs she was not trustworthy
News.content:
THE co-author of the court clerk who caused Alex Murdaugh’s conviction to be overturned has revealed some of the red flags that arose during their book writing process.

Becky Hill, the clerk of court who tried to sway the jury toward a guilty verdict to secure a book deal in the 2023 Murdaugh trial, has been brought back into the spotlight after the once-prominent lawyer’s conviction was overturned.





Murdaugh was convicted of fatally shooting his wife, Maggie, and youngest son, Paul, at their 21-acre estate in June 2021.

However, his conviction was overturned in May 2026 after the South Carolina Supreme Court justices said Hill “placed her fingers on the scales of justice, thereby denying Murdaugh his right to a fair trial by an impartial jury.”



While serving as clerk of court in Colleton County, Hill came up with the idea to write a book about the trial, which she later published alongside veteran journalist Neil Gordon.

The book, Behind the Doors of Justice: The Murdaugh Murders, was later pulled from Amazon after Gordon discovered Hill had plagiarized the first 12 pages of the book.

read more on becky hill OBSTRUCT JUSTICE How 'fame-seeking' clerk torpedoed Alex Murdaugh's murder conviction

Speaking exclusively with The U.S. Sun, Gordon said he was left feeling “a lot of different emotions” knowing someone he had worked with so closely had sparked the possibility of a retrial.

“It was very sad. I mean, the way everything started out was so exciting, putting the book together and our families getting to know each other and writing the book and having it, you know, opening the box of books the first time and putting in a lot of hard work.



“And then things just month by month started to unravel. I learned that she plagiarized the chapter of the book and then there were allegations that she violated some ethics within the clerk of court’s office. And then there were some criminal charges.

“It really is really sad. And I, you know, I can’t imagine what she must be thinking, hearing that she’s the cause. I mean, there was no doubt the way the justices wrote the ruling that she is the cause of a new trial.”

Gordon revealed that he was introduced to Hill by his wife, Melissa, who was a trial watcher. Hill confided in Melissa, telling her that she was interested in writing a book and already had a title in mind.

Gordon and Hill instantly hit it off, first meeting over the phone to discuss the book before they met in person and began the book-writing process through in-person visits, Zoom and email.

“She struck me as someone with Southern hospitality and very grandmotherly and very pleasant,” Gordon said.



The author and journalist from Augusta, Georgia, revealed that the pair were working quickly through the book, with deadline pressure creeping up on both of them as they hoped to get the book out before Netflix released a documentary on the case in September 2023.

The deadline pressure appeared to weigh heaviest on Hill, who cited it as the reason why she plagiarized a BBC reporter’s article in their book.

Gordon learned about the plagiarism after Hill’s emails were published following an open records request. A BBC reporter accidentally sent Hill a draft of her article, mixing up Hill’s email address with one of her editor’s who was also named Rebecca.



Gordon revealed in his 2024 book Trial Watchers that he picked up on some red flags when he initially read the chapter but brushed them off.

Some alarm bells rang after he noticed the draft was sent over via Google Drive when Hill always opted for Microsoft Word.

Another odd bit was that one of the subjects interviewed was a former colleague of Gordon’s, and when he mentioned that, Hill replied, “I’ll have to Google him.”

“Why did we all miss it? We all liked Becky. We all admired her Southern charm. We marveled at how she ran the ‘trial of the century.’ We trusted Becky,” Gordon wrote in Trial Watchers: Why we’re obsessed watching true crime from OJ and Casey to the “Miss Becky” and Murdaugh drama.

“I just thought it was really good writing,” Gordon told The U.S. Sun.



“And it was so good that the editor read it and said, this is different from the rest of the book. This is not really in Becky’s voice, but it’s really well done.”

He went public with the plagiarism allegations, sharing his side of the story with reporters. But before the news broke, Gordon gave Hill a heads-up that morning.

“I think that might have been my way of trying to encourage her to take responsibility for what she did and that it would be better to be transparent than again, stay silent like she did when there were allegations, ethics violations and other allegations,” he told The U.S. Sun.



When Gordon first noticed similarities between the reporter’s article and the preface of Behind the Doors of Justice, he pressed Hill for answers.

“I tried to give her an opportunity to reflect upon it. And she came up with some lame excuses or responses,” he told The U.S. Sun, adding that Hill claimed the reporter gave her permission to use it.

Gordon spoke with the BBC reporter, who said she asked Hill to delete the email after realizing her mistake.

Hill told her co-author that she wanted the writing to be a placeholder as she knew they needed more content, but then she got busy and forgot about it.

“I don’t believe that at all,” Gordon said.



“And she was a school teacher, by the way. And the biggest thing that school teachers make sure is the kids don’t copy somebody else’s work or the kids don’t go on the internet and use somebody else’s work that’s not theirs. So she knew better.”



When the jury tampering allegations first came out against Hill, Gordon had been quick to defend her.

“I felt like I had to, in a way, and some of it was for selfish or survival type reasons. We had worked so hard on the book,” he said.

“And because my name was on the book, whether I liked it or not, I was tied to Becky. And so I thought it was important to get out in front of this situation.”

With his name on the book, addressing the plagiarism was also important to him.

“I felt like the first 12 pages were was fraudulent. It was a fraud. And I was incredibly disappointed,” Gordon said.



Gordon said he had some concerns about conflicts of interest with Hill working on county time to promote the book after she did an interview in her clerk of courts office.

“I mean, this shows an incredible either lack of judgment or superwoman complex that she was untouchable,” he said.

Gordon explained that his family and Hill’s grew close during the book writing process, and despite all that went down he believes she is a sweet Southern lady like Aunt Bee from The Andy Griffith Show.



“I think there are several sides to Becky. At her core, I believe she is a graceful Southern lady with a lot of charm and nuances of sweet tea and, you know, come spend some time over here and, you know, use the rocking chair and such,” he said.

“And I believe that’s sincere. I definitely do.”

“[Becky] was sort of grandmotherly to me, even though I’m actually older than her,” Gordon told The U.S. Sun. “I kind of looked at her in that realm and as did my daughter, Lindy, as well.”

“When she would stay over, Lindy would, you know, climb into bed with her and they would, you know, read a story or what have you. So it was a very close relationship.”

Gordon said that Hill has a “tremendous support system,” but he can’t “imagine her going to the grocery store in Walterboro, her hometown.”



Gordon revealed he was not surprised by Murdaugh’s conviction being overturned.

“I expected it, actually.” he said. “It was evident to me they were very concerned about Becky’s conduct.”

Becky ultimately pleaded guilty to four state charges of obstruction of justice, perjury and misconduct in office, saying there was “no excuse” for her mistakes as she was handed three years of probation and required to complete 100 hours of community service.

Gordon said he has concerns about a retrial in Colleton County.

“I think it’s a mistake retrying Alex Murdaugh in Colleton County. I question whether anyone in the state of South Carolina doesn’t have an opinion on his guilt or innocence.



“But certainly in Walterboro with that level of scrutiny, everyone is very aware of the trial and I believe would have an opinion of it. So I don’t know how they pick jurors from that area, to be honest with you.

“I don’t think there will be a different outcome [in the retrial],” he added.

Gordon said he is no longer in contact with Hill or her husband, Tommy, but is open to speaking with her again.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I believe in giving people grace. I mean, we all make mistakes. No question about it,” he said.

“It just hadn’t been the right time. I think she’s been in so much legal trouble and police trouble and all of that. And so maybe when the dust settles a bit, probably after the trial, the retrial, maybe we’ll maybe we’ll try to make amends.”

News.title: Lammy’s gone soft with pathetic criminal responsibility plan… he’ll create an army of untouchable child crooks for gangs
News.content:
WE all know that kids are growing up faster than ever before – they’re even reaching puberty at an earlier age and the tween years are all but gone.

That’s why Labour plans to lower the voting age to 16, because they’re seen as such bright, mature young sparks.





But David Lammy doesn’t seem to have got that memo.

The Justice Secretary wants the age of criminal responsibility to be raised from ten to as high as 14 to reflect “modern understanding of childhood, vulnerability and development in today’s society”.

So, essentially, he now wants to give kids the green light to cause havoc.

Which is pathetic. We have all seen what they can be like from an early age. Intimidating little brats with their balaclavas on racing through the park on their electric scooters without any consideration for those in their path.

The rampaging primary school kids shoving nicked sweets into their pockets, throwing stones or scrawling graffiti on walls.

What’s really terrifying is the ones with knives, the ones who attack, the ones who torment old people in the park.

I admit I have a particular bee in my bonnet about it because one feral terror recently crashed on to the actual bonnet of my car.

He was with a gang of lads on his e-bike, with the obligatory scarf pulled up over his nose, and ploughed into my stationary motor.





As he rolled off my bonnet and flopped to the floor, his mask dropped with him. He was about 11.

Bystanders oddly rushed to this child’s aid while I took his photo. He ran off, then turned around and flicked the Vs.

A decent punishment would have knocked more sense into him than that thud on the floor ever could.

Thankfully, coppers do have the power to deal with rotten eggs like this to try to stop them stuffing up their lives, halt them from causing further harm to others or contaminating the decent children around them.

Naughty kids know that threat is real. But this review of youth justice would mean many would no longer face arrest, charge or prosecution by the police.

It’s as though Lammy has lost his backbone.

He’s gone soft at a time when the strong arm of the law is already dwindling. This would just make matters worse.

Of course, most of us think our kids are little angels. And many are.

But there are children who really would have got away with murder if Lammy’s ridiculous new proposal had been in place.

Like the two 12-year-old boys who fatally attacked 19-year-old Shawn Seesahai with a machete in a Wolverhampton park just three years ago.



Back in 1968, 11-year-old Mary Bell was convicted of the manslaughter of two young boys in Newcastle.

I was a trainee reporter when little James Bulger went missing on Merseyside in 1993.

I knocked on doors trying to help find the toddler, I was there when the community ground to a halt with shock when it became clear that ten-year-olds Jon Venables and Robert Thompson had abducted him from a shopping centre before torturing and killing him on a railway line.

Years later, I sat down with his mum Denise and witnessed first-hand the heartbreak primary school children can cause.

This week, she condemned this potential law change, saying it was a “dangerous move” and what we really need is tougher justice to prevent children committing adult crimes.

I couldn’t agree more.

Because by raising the age of criminality, we would also be putting many young children at risk from adults who would want to prey on them, too.

County lines gang bosses will be rubbing their hands with glee at the thought of playing modern-day Fagins, recruiting an army of young kids who are so untouchable from prosecution they are priceless to them.

And where is the justice in creating a generation of children who fear gang bosses more than the law?

VID CRITICS COULD LEARN A LOT FROM THE GC



YOU’VE got to love The GC – a larger-than-life I’m A Celeb quitter and all-round bubbly reality TV star.

But some people really have had it in for Gemma Collins since she collaborated with the Department for Education to promote post-16 education on social media.

And I don’t get it. In a series of videos she heads into their offices and shouts: “What are we doing to help the children?” before being invited to meet Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson.

The video is ridiculous, granted, but the abuse she’s got really isn’t justified.

She’s been slammed for having one GCSE and by parents of SEND children who say the comedy stunt is “tone-deaf” and an insulting mockery of an ongoing classroom crisis.

But like it or not, thanks to her 2.3million followers, The GC can get people to listen to her. Plus, she did it all for free because she wants to make a difference. Surely she deserves an A+ for effort.

PETE’S KYLIE GOOF

WHAT a career Kylie Minogue has had.



In Neighbours she proved dungarees, tomboys and girl-next-door types could be sexy.

We could skive school to watch it at 1pm and then jump on our beanbags at 5.30pm to watch it again. In the UK, 16million tuned in daily.

But, in new Netflix show Kylie, Pete Waterman says of the time Kylie turned up to record at the Stock Aitken and Waterman studios: “I had no idea who this girl was. We had Rick Astley, the world’s biggest artist.”

He was the only man in Britain who didn’t know her. Well done, Pete.

TRAVEL SAFELY JUDITH

WISH You Were Here…? presenter Judith Chalmers was to my generation what a TikTok holiday influencer is to the Gen Z of today.

I’m such a fan of holidays that some of my closest friends still dub me “Judith”.

So I was sad to hear of her passing this week aged 90.

But as her family put it, she left behind “a giant suitcase of the happiest of memories”.

She also visited more than 120 countries and went to far-flung resorts when the rest of us were still feeling tropical about a fortnight in Benidorm.



Not a bad life. Not a bad life at all.

NOT SO D-ANDY

I KEEP getting asked as “a northerner” what I think about Andy Burnham.

My answer is simple: He needs a stylist. Yes, yes, I get the whole, “Aren’t I a cool man of the people?” vibe.

But he looks as though he’s been vomited up by JD Sports.

Sometimes get yourself in a suit with a shirt and tie man, if you’re serious about the top job.

A quick trip to the Trafford Centre and you’ll be sorted out in minutes.

BETTER OFF RED SOME scientific bods have come up with a new report that says we need around nine to ten hours of exercise a week to see a substantial reduction in the risk of stroke or heart attack. I’m not quite sure how any normal working person could actually cram that in. There’s two options in my house – either A) go to the gym every night for two hours after putting my son to bed or B) ignore the advice completely and just relax with a glass of red wine. As both are good for your heart, I think I’ll opt for the latter.

DEVASTATING news this week if you’re a fellow Mini Cheddars fan. In a Which? report, they came out as being one of the fattiest crisp-like snacks.

I’ve always been sold by the “oven baked, never fried” on the packaging and therefore munched them with gusto.

Proof you should never judge a book by its cover – or a snack by its selling tactics.



MOBLAND is coming back for a third series but Tom Hardy has reportedly been fired and won’t appear alongside Pierce Brosnan and Dame Helen Mirren.

It’s said to be down to a series of clashes with producers on set.

But without his rugged gangster/soft-hearted hubby character Harry, the entire thing seems a bit pointless.

News.title: Burnham & Streeting are shallow careerists who have no real principles… they will say anything to get the keys to No10
News.content:
“DOES the Prime Minister agree with Andy Burnham when he says we should rejoin the European Union?” asked Tory MP Esther McVey.

“Or does he agree with Andy Burnham when he says we should not rejoin the European Union?”



The mischievous McVey makes an excellent point.

Andy Burnham, proud and passionate supporter of the European project, is suddenly comically coy about his pro-Brussels beliefs as he campaigns to become MP for Brexit-voting Makerfield.

Meanwhile, back in Westminster, Wes Streeting — Andy’s great rival to replace Keir Starmer in 10 Downing Street — boldly proclaims Brexit a “catastrophic mistake” as he attempts to ingratiate himself with Labour MPs and party activists.



But in his own special way, Streeting in Westminster is being as laughably bashful as Burnham in Makerfield.

Because Streeting never reveals what price he would be prepared to pay to get our country back inside the warm embrace of Brussels.

Would he happily give up the pound for the euro?

Would he cheerfully kiss goodbye to the £5billion-a-year rebate negotiated by Maggie Thatcher?

Would Wes gladly be part of the Schengen Area, the free-for-all travel zone of 29 European countries who have abolished controls at their mutual borders? Would he welcome much higher immigration?



Enough with the mealy-mouthed prevarication!

Enough of the weasel words!

As they dream of choosing the curtains for 10 Downing Street, we need to be told — what do these little men who want to be the ultimate big cheese actually believe?

At the moment, we have no idea. Keir Starmer won a General Election based on a pro-business, pro-growth platform of stability, competence and national prosperity.

A pack of lies.



Now the wannabe PMs are using the same filthy little playbook.

“Promise the suckers anything!”

Wes Streeting has been such a Blairite moderate in the past that he enjoyed selfies with Peter Mandelson.

But now Wes has to win over the comrades in Parliament and his party, he comes on like a Corbynista.

Streeting’s latest stunt is a £12billion soak-the-rich “wealth tax”, even though multiple millionaires have already fled our Socialist paradise, and even though all the evidence suggests that a “wealth tax” would actually make us all poorer (because when you drive the rich abroad, you end up with 100 per cent of nothing).



Oooh, you’re such a left-wing firebrand, Wes.

And on the doorsteps of Makerfield, it is unclear if King of the North Andy Burnham is sharing his deeply-held views on trans rights with those working-class constituents.

As recently as 2022, this bargain basement Robb Stark was loftily proclaiming that men who identify as women should be allowed access to female toilets, and that opposing this madness was “a minority view”.

Just guessing here, but I bet Burnham is not expressing his support for trans rights on the mean streets of Makerfield.

In fact, he is already back-pedalling so desperately that you can see the nervous sweat stains on his Rab C. Nesbitt white T-shirt.



And these hypocritical clowns want to be our next Prime Minister.

They are shallow careerists.

They are all about the vibes, baby.

Wes Streeting tells the lefties exactly what they want to hear in Westminster. Andy Burnham does the same with working-class voters in Makerfield.

Burnham is too much of a gutless coward to tell us if he really thinks a woman can have a penis.



Streeting is too much of a spineless scaredy cat to tell us if the UK would have to crawl to get back in the EU.

As Groucho Marx would have told you, these are Wes and Andy’s deeply held principles, and if you don’t like them — don’t worry. They have others!

DOING AN ANITA? NO, TREVI CLOWN IS JUST DUMB

A FULLY clothed New Zealand tourist launches himself into Rome’s Trevi Fountain and then splashes about like a baby seal on bath night.



Video of the incident went viral in Italy, provoking national outrage at this mindless desecration of Rome’s iconic landmark.

Especially when the Kiwi clown got off with a fine of 500 euros.

“They [tourists] think they can do anything they want,” fumed one irate Italian. “The fine should be 5,000 euros.”

A few commentators suggested that the pea-brained tourist was trying to emulate Anita Ekberg when she famously cavorted in the Trevi Fountain in Federico Fellini’s classic 1960 film, La Dolce Vita.

I am not convinced that this soggy moron is a Fellini fan. Dumb and Dumber is probably more his thing.



KEEP MUM, HARRY

WHO should be England manager – Thomas Tuchel or Harry Maguire’s mum?

Herr Tuchel has left England stalwart Harry “Slabhead” Maguire out of our World Cup squad.

Harry didn’t like it, but he graciously wished the lads well.

Zoe Maguire, Harry’s mum, was less forgiving.



“Absolutely disgusted,” Mum posted on X.

England have a squad that gives everyone something to complain about.

To me, the glaring error is leaving Cole Palmer home because – apart from his other manifest gifts – he is one of the greatest penalty takers in Premier League history.

Ice man Cole has taken 19 penalties in the Premier League for Chelsea. He has missed . . . once.

Like Harry Maguire’s mum, I will miss seeing some of the men who did not make the cut – Slabhead, Phil Foden, Trent Alexander-Arnold and penalty king Cole.



And I hope, for Herr Tuchel’s sake, England do not miss any penalties.

SHOW’S BIG FOR SMALLS

KNICKER experts inform us that Sydney Sweeney has been wearing her very own lingerie brand Syrn – pronounced “siren” – on Euphoria as her character Cassie attempts to raise money for her wedding on adult site Only Fans.

Naked Syd wrestles with a snake and struggles to be contained by a corset.

For a date night with Jacob Elordi’s character Nate, she sports dog ears, a collar and lead and laps water from a bowl on the floor.



It’s an undeniably exciting moment.

Will Nate have sex with her or take her for a walk in the park?

Yet no matter how often Sweeney takes her kit off, and no matter how hard Euphoria tries to shock, the most remarkable thing about the show will always be the number of A-list stars it has made.

Jacob Elordi. Sydney Sweeney. Zendaya.

Yes, they had all been knocking around before Euphoria.



But after Euphoria, they are all ensured a Hollywood career that will endure for decades.

That is what is truly shocking about Euphoria.

There is no show in the history of television that has created so many big stars.

Or featured so many small pants.

EARLY GOAL



HERE in North London, the best thing about the night Arsenal celebrated their first Premier League title in 22 years was the morning after.

The new day was breaking over the Emirates and only a few stragglers were left waiting for the first Tube or bus home.

Then, four weary, exhilarated Arsenal players bowled up for a stroll around the stadium.

Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Jurrien Timber and Eberechi Eze will cost you close to a half a billion quid on the transfer market.

By turning up at the Arsenal stadium at dawn, those players created memories that are priceless.



CHANCELLOR Rachel Reeves has unveiled a Summer Savings package that will mean discounts at fairs, theme parks and zoos.

So you will still not be able to pay your energy bill.

But I bet the monkeys are adorable.

MURMURINGS of discontent among the Strictly fanbase as the new line-up of presenters is unveiled.



Yes, we will all miss Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.

But I don’t know how anyone can complain too much about a team that includes pro dancer Johannes Radebe, Emma Willis and, er, Austin Powers.

AS she celebrated the eighth anniversary of her marriage to Prince Harry, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, shared 24 informal, intimate photographs with her 4.6million followers on Instagram.

Dancing. Snogging. Baking.



A bit more snogging, just to prove how deliriously happy they are.

Are Meghan and Harry still desperate to protect their privacy?

Because I can’t think of another couple on planet Earth who seem quite so pathetically desperate for publicity.

News.title: Jewish children told by headteacher to swap kippahs for baseball caps on Legoland school trip to avoid being targeted
News.content:
JEWISH children were told to swap their traditional skull caps for baseball hats in case they were targeted on a school trip to Legoland.

A headteacher made the drastic decision to conceal their heritage at the theme park amid a horrific rise in antisemitism.





One of the parents whose children went on the May 5 trip revealed that, as well as removing their kippah caps, the North London school pupils were also told not to wear uniform.

One of the parents, teacher and rabbi Doron Birnbaum, 35, who has three children aged ten, seven and three, said: “My eldest two went on the trip to Legoland Windsor.

“They were told not to look visibly Jewish as they could not be kept safe if they did.”

Mr Birnbaum added: “It was heartbreaking for me, I sent my son out without a kippah on, and I go everywhere with my kippah on.”

In the past month there have been several police investigations launched into assaults on Jewish children in North London.

In Finchley, a car mounted the kerb and sped towards three 14-year-old schoolboys.

In Belsize Park, a group of Jewish children were assaulted and subjected to abusive language by youths from another school.

And in Stamford Hill, an 11-year-old boy was pushed into a shop shutter while riding his scooter.



There is no suggestion Legoland was aware of any threats.

News.title: Cops probing claims a child was sexually abused and tortured by paedo ring in Surrey after Epstein Files allegations
News.content:
POLICE are probing claims that a child was sexually abused and tortured by a paedophile ring in Surrey, based on allegations in the Epstein Files.

Officers are investigating two separate claims of child sex abuse said to have taken place between the mid-1980s and 2000.





It is understood cops are searching for evidence and have interviewed the alleged victims.

No arrests have been made.

One of the complainants came forward when the force appealed for witnesses after the publication of a redacted FBI report in the Jeffrey Epstein files.

It alleged human trafficking and sexual assault in Virginia Water, Surrey, in the mid-1990s.

The individual claimed they were abused at “paedophile ring parties” when they were aged six to eight.

In the Files, the FBI was told the then-Duke of York was present at a private house in the affluent Thorpe Green hamlet.

The unnamed person claimed they sustained “permanent injuries” to their ribs, hip and leg when they were hit by a car.

They said the vehicle’s hood figurine broke off and they buried it to be used as “recoverable evidence”.



EPSTEIN CALLS TO RAMPTON Exclusive by Emma Parry JEFFREY Epstein made mysterious phone calls to high-security psychiatric unit Rampton, raising fears that he may have been in contact with twisted Jimmy Savile. Phone records in the Epstein Files, uncovered by The Sun on Sunday, show the billionaire paedo made 24 calls to the tiny Nottinghamshire village from 2004 to 2005. A 2014 NHS report found four incidents of inappropriate sexual behaviour from Savile there, including one with a five-year-old child. The Trust was asked for coment.

The individual also said they had “medical records” of trauma sustained in the alleged sex attack.

On another occasion they reportedly escaped naked and asked for help from a community of nearby Irish travellers.

The document also includes allegations of abuse at Frogmore Cottage on the Windsor estate.

The alleged victim claimed Epstein associate Ghislaine Maxwell restrained them, before they were “tortured with electrical shocks”.



They also said paedo financier Epstein molested and attempted to rape them in Florida.

It is understood that no potential suspects have yet been interviewed and the allegations have not been proven.

Surrey Police said: “We take all reports of sexual offending seriously and will work to identify any reasonable lines of enquiry to verify information or establish corroborating evidence.”

Andrew, who was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, has always denied any wrongdoing.

News.title: Donald Trump's rambling Truth Social post about Iran war deal in full as 'questions remain'
News.content:
Donald Trump's rambling Truth Social post about Iran war deal in full as 'questions remain'

Donald Trump has said the details of a deal with Iran will include an opening of the Strait of Hormuz - the US president said a deal has 'largely been negotiated'

View 4 Images Trump has said a deal is close (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump has said a deal with Iran has “largely been negotiated”.

‌



The US President said in a post on his Truth Social media platform that the “final aspects and details” of a deal are “currently being discussed” but are set to be announced soon. He said this will include an opening of the Strait of Hormuz, the vital artery for the world’s oil supply which has been effectively closed by Iran since the war began, sending oil prices skyrocketing.

‌



It is not the first time a deal has been described as close, however.

‌



He said he had spoken with leaders from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Bahrain, and separately with Israel.

View 4 Images An Iranian flag flutters in the wind as ships remain anchored on May 16, 2026 in the Strait of Hormuz near Larak Island (Image: Getty Images)

He described it as a “Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE” that still must be finalised by the United States, Iran and the other countries that participated in Saturday’s talks.

‌



The final form any deal is agreed may raise questions over the Trump administration's decision to embark on military action in Iran. With the global economy hurting following the closure of the strait and clear tensions between the US and its allies over their refusal to join military action, as well as Trump's campaign promises to end the war, the aftermath is likely to raise questions for Trump.

The Mirror has approached the White House for comment.

In Trump's post, there was no mention of Iran’s nuclear programme and highly enriched uranium, which Iran has sought to discuss later.

‌



The United States and Iran were closing in on a deal to end the war, a regional official with direct knowledge of the Pakistan-led mediation efforts said earlier on Saturday, after the US weighed a new round of attacks on the Islamic Republic.

View 4 Images The Strait of Hormuz and lines representing global shipping lanes (Image: Alones Creative via Getty Images)

The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, cautioned that “last-minute disputes” could blow up the efforts.

‌



He said the potential deal would include an official declaration of the war’s end, with two-month negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

The Strait of Hormuz would be reopened and the US would end its blockade of Iran’s ports.

Iran, meanwhile, had signalled “narrowing differences” in negotiations with the US after Pakistan’s army chief held more talks in Tehran, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told journalists in India that “there’s been some progress made” and “there may be news later today”.

‌



Both Iran and the US emphasised their key positions and have warned of the risks of resuming attacks and disrupting their ceasefire.

Mr Rubio repeated the US’s stance that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon and must turn over its highly enriched uranium, and the Strait of Hormuz must be open.

Iran state TV earlier quoted Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei as describing the draft as a “framework agreement” and adding: “We want this to include the main issues required for ending the imposed war and other issues of essential importance to us.

‌



View 4 Images Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (Image: ISNA/AFP via Getty Images)

“Then, over a reasonable time span, between 30 and 60 days, details are discussed and ultimately a final agreement is reached.”

He said the Strait of Hormuz is among the topics discussed.

‌



Mr Baghaei told Iran’s official IRNA news agency: “Over the past week, the trend has been toward narrowing differences.”

He added that nuclear issues are not part of the current negotiations.

“Our focus at this stage is on ending the war on all fronts, including Lebanon,” he said, adding that lifting sanctions on Tehran “has explicitly been included in the text and remains our fixed position”.

‌



The Iranian-backed Hezbollah’s Al-Manar TV reported that the Lebanese militant group’s leader, Naim Kassim, received a letter from Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying Tehran will not abandon its allies.

There is a fragile, US-brokered ceasefire in the Israel-Hezbollah war in Lebanon, a conflict that began two days after the Iran war started. Limiting Tehran’s support for armed proxies in the region has been a stated goal in the war, along with targeting its ballistic missile programme.

Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, the lead negotiator in historic face-to-face talks with the US last month in Islamabad, said Iran has rebuilt its military assets and if Mr Trump resumes attacks, the result would be “more crushing and more bitter” than at the start of the war.

‌



State TV said he spoke after meeting with Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir, who also met with Araghchi, President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials. Qatar sent a senior official to Tehran to support Pakistan’s efforts.

Mr Trump earlier said he was holding off on a military strike against Iran because “serious negotiations” were underway, and at the request of allies in the Middle East.

The US President has repeatedly set deadlines for Tehran and then backed off. The US and Israel sparked the war with attacks on February 28, cutting short nuclear talks with Iran.

‌



Tehran retaliated by effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the region’s oil, natural gas and fertiliser, causing global economic pain.

The US then blockaded Iranian ports, with US Central Command saying on Saturday that its forces had turned away more than 100 commercial vessels and disabled four since the blockade began on April 13.

Trump's Truth Social post in full

"I am in the Oval Office at the White House where we just had a very good call with President Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud, of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, of The United Arab Emirates, Emir Tamim bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani, and Minister Ali al-Thawadi, of Qatar, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir Ahmed Shah, of Pakistan, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, of Türkiye, President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, of Egypt, King Abdullah II, of Jordan, and King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, of Bahrain, concerning the Islamic Republic of Iran, and all things related to a Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE.

Article continues below

"An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed. Separately, I had a call with Prime Minister Bibi Netanyahu, of Israel, which, likewise, went very well.

"Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly. In addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

News.title: US Iran war live: Peace deal would see Strait of Hormuz opened 'largely agreed'
News.content:
"Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly"

A peace deal between the US and Iran has been 'largely agreed'.

Donald Trump posted on Truth Social saying: "An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries, as listed. Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly. In addition to many other elements of the Agreement, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened."

Senior officials on both sides have reportedly signed off on the proposal, with final approval now resting with national leaders, according to the Washington Times. The deal is intended to transform the current six-week ceasefire into a lasting peace agreement.

Reuters news agency says the US president will hold a phone call tomorrow with leaders from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Jordan, Egypt, Turkey and Pakistan.

News.title: UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come
News.content:
Weather forecasting models suggest the UK could see temperatures rise to 35C as a heatwave grips the country - the Met Office has forecast 33C highs for Monday

UK weather live: Heatwave brings hottest day of year – Met Office says more to come

The Met Office has confirmed the hottest day of the year so far today.

The village of Frittenden, in Kent, hit 30.3C on Saturday and the forecasting body said temperatures are still rising. Before now, Friday had seen the year's warmest temperatures when highs of 28.4C were measured in Heathrow, Cambridge and Cranwell in Lincolnshire.

It comes as the UK faces a days-long heatwave with the Met Office forecasting record breaking temperatures for May. Heat health alerts have been issued by the UKHSA across England.

The UKV weather model now suggests the East of England could reach 35C at around 3pm on Tuesday. And it shows 15 counties at 33C or more - Gloucestershire, Warwickshire, Staffordshire, Norfolk, Suffolk, Leicestershire, Northamptonshire, Cambridgeshire, Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Essex, Surrey, and Berkshire.

News.title: Under pressure Putin shows 'something big' in latest nuclear sabre-rattling move
News.content:
Under pressure Putin shows 'something big' in latest nuclear sabre-rattling move

Maligned Russian leader Vladimir Putin presided over joint military drills in Belarus in another showing of strength, but he faces increasing pressure at home and in the war

View 5 Images Putin is facing an increasingly tricky situation in Ukraine (Image: Mikhail Metzel/Pool Sputnik Krem)

Experts have warned of “something big” taking place as Vladimir Putin showed off his nuclear arsenal again.

‌



The maligned Russian leader presided over joint military drills in Belarus, alongside his “lapdog” counterpart Alexander Lukashenko, this week. Russian arsenals in Belarus include its latest intermediate-range nuclear-capable Oreshnik missile system.

‌



On Thursday, Putin said it was “important to further boost the level of readiness of strategic and tactical nuclear forces”, as drills including the firing of a hypersonic missile were carried out.

‌



Exercises involved over 200 missile launchers, 73 surface warships, 13 submarines and 140 aircraft along with 64,000 troops, the Russian Defence Ministry said. The drills, which were ministry said was for the “preparation and use of nuclear forces under the threat of aggression”, included eight submarines armed with nuke-laden intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs).

View 5 Images Belarus' President Alexander Lukashenko attending nuclear drills on May 21 (Image: Belarusian Presidential Press Se)

The manoeuvres featured a broad assortment of short and medium-range weapons. Unlike the intercontinental missiles that can destroy entire cities, tactical nuclear weapons intended for use against troops on the battlefield are less powerful. They include aerial bombs and warheads for short and medium-range missiles and artillery munitions.

‌



Russian armed forces test-fired Yars and Sineva ICBMs, as well as medium-range sea-launched Zircon and air-launched Kinzhal missiles, noting that all missiles hit their designated practice targets. Belarusian troops test-fired a short-range Iskander ballistic missile inside Russia.

“Something big is taking place, something that will be significant for international politics in general, and for mass media, including the very supply of nuclear arms,” Bremen University researcher Nikolay Mitrokhin warned, speaking to Al-Jazeera.

Putin has repeatedly deployed ‘sabre-rattling’ rhetoric involving the use of nuclear weapons since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

‌



View 5 Images Rescuers work at a residential building partially destroyed following Russian drones and missiles strikes in Kyiv on May 1 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

He has said that Moscow will retain control of its nuclear weapons deployed in Belarus, which borders Ukraine and NATO members Latvia, Lithuania and Poland, but would allow its ally to select the targets in case of conflict.

Since the full-scale war, the Russian president changed Moscow’s nuclear doctrine so that any nation’s conventional attack on Russia that is supported by a nuclear power will be considered a joint attack on his country. It was a change by the Kremlin clearly aimed at discouraging the West from allowing Ukraine to strike Russia with longer-range weapons and appears to significantly lower the threshold for the possible use of Moscow’s nuclear arsenal.

‌



The use of nuclear weapons in Ukraine would be met with a "devastating" response, NATO secretary general Mark Rutte said this week. The drills this week were a response to a “threat of aggression”, according to Minsk and Moscow. It is not clear what the perceived threat they were referring to was.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned that Russia may try to “drag Belarus into an expansion of the war”. Russia’s presence in Belarus created an obvious pressure point for Kyiv and Zelensky has said there are “additional tasks for our intelligence regarding this threat”. Belarus was previously used as a launch point for Russian forces in February 2022.

View 5 Images Zelensky has warned Russia will pull Belarus into the war (Image: UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



But warnings of a new offensive into northern Ukraine have been tempered. The Kyiv-based Penta think-tank said the number of Russian forces in Belarus is “insufficient” for a new attack.

Putin is what a number of analysts are suggesting is an increasingly tricky situation in Ukraine. His attempts to sell the war to the public as a far-away ‘special operation’ could be increasingly undermined by continued Ukrainian strikes on Russian infrastructure.

There is further pressure at home, with Russian discontent at a crackdown on internet access, and problems in the war. Last month, Ukraine gained more territory than it lost for the first time in two years, the US-based National Security Journal has said Russia has lost “more soldiers than it can replace” for five months in a row.

‌



Its invasion continues to falter, but there is so far little to suggest its growing manpower problem is at a critical stage. The same can be said for the Russian economy, although its slowing down has clearly irked Putin, who blasted officials for not coming up with a plan.

View 5 Images A prayer house of a local Protestant community of Evangelical Christian Baptists burns following a Russian air attack in Balakliia, Kharkiv region, Ukraine, Saturday, May 23 (Image: Ukrainian Emergency Service via)

Overnight, a Ukrainian drone attack caused a fire at another Russian oil terminal, local officials in Russia’s Krasnodar region said on Saturday, in what appeared to be the latest attack on Moscow’s vital oil industry. Authorities in the city of Novorossiysk said falling drone debris sparked a fire at an oil terminal, injuring two people.

‌



Russia’s Astra news outlet said Ukrainian drones struck the Sheskharis oil terminal and depot, the terminus for Russian state-controlled pipeline company Transneft’s main oil pipelines in the region. Images posted by Astra appeared to show smoke rising above the oil terminal, but they could not be verified.

On Saturday afternoon, Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces had struck the Sheskharis oil terminal overnight. “The facility provides shipment of oil and oil products for export and is involved in meeting the needs of the Russian army,” the General Staff wrote on Telegram, adding that Ukrainian forces had also hit a tanker in the Black Sea belonging to Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet”.

Ukraine has expanded its mid- and long-range strike capabilities, deploying drone and missile technology that it has developed domestically to battle Russia’s four-year-old invasion. Attacks on Russian oil assets that play a key part in funding the invasion have become almost daily occurrences.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, the death toll from a Ukrainian drone strike overnight into Friday on a college dormitory building in Starobilsk, a city in Ukraine’s Russia-occupied Luhansk region, rose to 18, the press service of Russia’s Ministry of Emergency Situations said. According to the ministry, 60 people were wounded in the attack.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday denounced the attack on the dormitory as a “crime” and ordered the military to submit its proposals for retaliation. He said there were no military or law enforcement facilities near the college.

At a UN Security Council emergency meeting on the strike, held at the request of Russia, Ukrainian Ambassador Andrii Melnyk denied his Russian counterpart’s accusations of war crimes, calling them a “pure propaganda show” and asserting that the May 22 operations “exclusively targeted the Russian war machine”.

News.title: Keir Starmer vows to ‘keep pushing forward’ as he defends record in office
News.content:
Keir Starmer vows to ‘keep pushing forward’ as he defends record in office

In a rallying cry as Andy Burnham seeks a return to parliament and Wes Streeting vowed to challenge the PM, Mr Starmer highlighted measures to ease the cost-of-living squeeze on families

View 2 Images Keir Starmer highlighted his own record (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

Keir Starmer has claimed efforts to cut costs, reduce net migration and boost growth show his “plan is working”.

‌



In a rallying cry as Andy Burnham seeks a return to parliament and Wes Streeting vowed to challenge the PM, Mr Starmer highlighted measures to ease the cost-of-living squeeze on families and vowed his Government will “keep pushing forward”.

‌



It comes in the face of nearly 100 Labour MPs calling for the PM to stand down in the wake of brutal election results earlier this month across English councils, Wales and Scotland.

‌



Mr Starmer, who has insisted he will not walk away from No 10 if the Greater Manchester Mayor wins the June 18 by-election and triggers a leadership contest, has sought to highlight his own record of delivery.

Rachel Reeves slashes VAT rate for summer attractions - from theme parks to zoos READ MORE :

View 2 Images It comes amid rumours of an Andy Burnham leadership challenge (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He said: “We now have the fastest-growing economy in the G7, net migration has fallen and NHS waiting lists are at their lowest level in three-and-a-half years. Our plan is working. And as summer begins, we are going further to bring down the cost of living and make life easier for families, so they have more room to enjoy it. This Government will keep pushing forward to deliver the change the country voted for.”

Office for National Statistics figures showed the economy grew by a higher-than-expected 0.6% over the first quarter, between January and March.

Figures this week also showed UK net migration dropped to an estimated 171,000 last year, the lowest level since the start of the coronavirus pandemic.

Article continues below

The most recent NHS England data shows the waiting list stood at 7.11 million treatments in March, a fall of 110,073 treatments from February.

It comes as Rachel Reeve slashed ticket prices for fairs, theme parks and zoos this summer to ease the cost of living burden on families. The Chancellor said VAT on summer attractions will be cut from 20% to 5% alongside children's meals in restaurants as part of a "Great British Summer Savings" scheme.

Estimated to cost around £300million, it will also include free bus travel for children between the ages of five and 15.

News.title: Carol Vorderman's brutal three-word takedown of Farage's Reform candidate for Makerfield
News.content:
Carol Vorderman's brutal three-word takedown of Farage's Reform candidate for Makerfield

Reform has stood by Robert Kenyon, a plumber and the candidate for the party in the upcoming Makerfield by-election, after comments he made about TV star Carol Vorderman resurfaced

View 3 Images Carol hit back at resurfaced social media comments by a Reform candidate (Image: Dave J Hogan/Getty Images)

Carol Vorderman has lashed out at a creepy sexual message by a Reform by-election candidate with a brutal three-word takedown.

‌



Reform UK candidate Robert Kenyon, who is standing to be the next MP for Makerfield in the upcoming by-election, backed up a degrading comment about the TV star along with other comments directed at women. Hitting back, Carol branded Nigel Farage’s candidate a “disgusting online abuser”.

‌



The campaign group HopeNotHate found Kenyon had two X accounts. One has been deleted and the other was suspended by X, HopeNotHate said.

‌



Reform has stood by Kenyon, a plumber, and has said his lack of “polish” could make him an effective MP.

View 3 Images Nigel Farage's party has stood by its candidate (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

"Fundamentally, Rob Kenyon is a misogynist,” Carol told The Mirror. "I wouldn't let him in my house if he was a local plumber in my area, not with what he's been posting online. There is always a pattern.”

‌



In 2021, an X user who wrote a degrading sexual message about Carol, which drew criticism from another person. To this, Kenyon responded by saying “he's only saying what we're all thinking”.

And another of the posts from the accounts referenced being blocked by the Sky Sports Rugby League account on X for comments about women's rugby.

Carol added: “He's been talking about how female rugby players 'handle their knockers', saying if it's not 't**s, and a**e', and he'd been blocked by the Sky Sports Rugby League Twitter page for his online behaviour.

‌



“It’s a torrent of abusive and vile language. Nobody knows why his X account was suspended. X has a very low bar for suspension, and the public should know and Reform should tell us why his account was suspended. What were his actions for this to have happened?

View 3 Images Reform candidate in the Makerfield by-election Robert Kenyon

"Last year the Victim's Commissioner said 'misogyny normalises violence against women and girls, normalises illegal harms such as harassment, abuse and stalking. And these harms manifest in both online and offline spaces'.”

‌



Carol emphasised the comments are not just Kenyon “being a lad”, adding he is “being a disgusting online abuser who became a Reform councillor three weeks ago”.

In response to HopeNotHate's investigation, a Reform UK spokesman said: “We fully back Cllr Kenyon. He is an excellent, local candidate who we are confident will be a superb MP for Makerfield.

“These comments were made before he was in politics. Rob isn’t a polished, professional politician and doesn’t speak like one. That’s precisely why he’ll be a straight-talking, effective voice for normal working people in Makerfield.”

‌



After being read Reform's response, Carol said: "So basically, it doesn't matter how misogynistic or otherwise he has been as far as Reform are concerned. And they didn't care that their MP James McMurdock had been put in jail for kicking his girlfriend outside a nightclub and that it hadn’t been declared. They simply don’t care at all."

A Labour Party spokesman said: "Robert Kenyon’s comments online are disgusting and show that he's not fit to represent Makerfield.

"From creepy remarks about women, to peddling baseless conspiracy theories, this is appalling stuff from a parliamentary candidate - on top of being Facebook friends with a fascist campaigner. Nigel Farage needs to explain why Reform UK selected him in the first place.”

‌



The first weekend of campaigning in Makerfield, meanwhile, got underway.

Andy Burnham, who is viewed as a challenger to Sir Keir Starmer in a potential Labour leadership race, launched his by-election campaign on Friday and promised he was not offering “more of the same”.

Allies of Mr Burnham have suggested he may not launch a bid for the party leadership immediately if he is successful in his attempt to return to Parliament in the June 18 contest.

‌



But Wes Streeting, who resigned from the Cabinet earlier this month, has openly talked about launching a campaign to oust Prime Minister Sir Keir.

The MP and former health secretary told reporters on Friday that he held off triggering a leadership race to give Mr Burnham time to tread a path back into the Commons.

In a pitch to voters, Greater Manchester Mayor Mr Burnham said: “I know my own party needs to change. We need to be better than we have been.

Article continues below

“A vote for me in this by-election is a vote to change Labour.”

Mr Burnham, who is also a former health secretary, later told reporters Labour has “space to be more radical” while honouring the party’s 2024 general election manifesto.

News.title: Hottest day of year as 30.5C recorded and temperatures set to soar
News.content:
Temperatures will continue to soar across the bank holiday weekend following the hottest day of the year so far on Saturday.

A high of 30.5C was recorded at Frittenden in Kent, beating Friday's maximum temperature of 28.4C at Heathrow in London, Cranwell in Lincolnshire and Cambridge.

The Met Office said it was very rare for the UK to record temperatures above 30C in May, with the last time being on 25 May 2012.

The heat is forecast to intensify throughout the long weekend, reaching heatwave criteria in a number of locations. Daytime highs are forecast to reach the upper 20s Celsius in many areas, with the low 30s Celsius likely in the week ahead.

Amber heat health alerts remain in effect for the Midlands, eastern and south-east England.

Amber alerts mean there is a risk of a significant impact across health and social care services, with children and those aged over 65 at risk of negative health implications.

The remainder of England is under yellow heat health alerts, meaning adverse weather is "likely to affect vulnerable groups".

News.title: Starmer urges TNT to make Champions League final free-to-air
News.content:
Sir Keir Starmer has called on TNT Sports to make next Saturday's Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris St-Germain free-to-air.

The UK prime minister has written to the broadcaster to "strongly urge you to reconsider" a decision to make the final available to subscribers only.

Every previous final since the Champions League format was introduced to the European Cup in 1992 has been made available to watch free of charge in the UK.

In a letter to TNT executives, Starmer wrote: "I was saddened to see that, for the first time since the competition started 34 years ago, TNT Sports has decided that [the fixture] will not be free to watch for football supporters here in the UK."

Last week, it was revealed that fans would need a subscription to watch all three European club finals, to which TNT holds the rights.

Starmer - who is an Arsenal fan - wrote: "The Champions League is the biggest club football competition in the world and rightly means a lot to fans in this country - the home of football.

"I am a firm believer that the final of this competition should remain free to watch, whether Arsenal have made it or not.

"Obviously, I want as many fellow fans as possible to be able to watch our team in this historic final for the first time in 20 years. However, this is bigger than that.

"This is about supporters of all teams coming together in living rooms and pubs in every corner of the country to watch the most elite players in Europe battle it out.

"Hard-working people should not have to worry about forking out for a subscription to watch a game of this magnitude.

"We should be putting supporters first. That is why I have already encouraged Fifa to do more to make tickets more affordable at this summer's World Cup.

"That is also why I want to strongly urge you to reconsider and make the final next Saturday free to watch for the millions of passionate football fans in this country."

Fans wanting to watch Aston Villa win the Europa League final last week needed a subscription, and the same will apply to those wanting to watch the Conference League final between Crystal Palace and Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday.

In a statement, TNT Sports said: "It has been a privilege to bring Uefa club competitions to sports fans across the UK throughout the season.

"Having three Premier League clubs reach the finals shows the strength of English football and something that we are proud to continue to support.

"We have made all three Uefa finals this year available from just Â£4.99, the price for a month-long subscription to HBO Max that also includes the great entertainment on the service. This represents exceptional value for fans to watch the conclusion of the competitions."

The Justice Department has confirmed that it removed news releases from its website that documented criminal cases related to January 6, 2021, when MAGA supporters fought police and stormed the U.S. Capitol, calling the material “partisan propaganda.”

The deleted pages included press releases that detailed charges, convictions and sentencing outcomes for defendants involved in the riot, when Trump supporters breached the Capitol in an effort to stop the certification of the 2020 election results after his loss to Joe Biden.

The changes drew attention after Washington Post reporter Meryl Kornfield posted before-and-after screenshots of the DOJ website on X on Friday, alleging the department was “quietly deleting info” as it prepares to distribute funds to people convicted in connection with the riot.

“Nothing ‘quiet’ about it,” the official DOJ Rapid Response account responded to Kornfield’s post. “We are proud to reverse the DOJ’s weaponization under the Biden administration. We will do everything in our power to make whole those who were persecuted for political purposes. This includes stripping DOJ’s website of partisan propaganda.”

Among the deleted materials were high-profile case summaries involving members of far-right groups such as the Proud Boys and Oath Keepers, who were previously convicted on charges including seditious conspiracy, Politico reports. Some of those convictions have since been vacated or dropped following recent Justice Department actions and court rulings.

The DOJ confirmed Friday that it removed news releases from its website documenting cases against people charged in connection with the January 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol ( Getty Images )

This is the latest step in the Trump administration’s effort to reshape the narrative around January 6.

On his first day back in office in January 2025, Trump issued sweeping clemency measures tied to the Capitol attack, pardoning, commuting sentences or directing the dismissal of cases involving more than 1,500 defendants. The actions covered a range of cases, including people convicted of serious assaults on police officers during the riot. Some of those convictions involved attackers who used improvised weapons such as flagpoles, a hockey stick and a crutch during the breach of the Capitol.

The Trump administration is also advancing a nearly $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund to compensate people it says were unfairly targeted by federal investigations, with eligibility potentially extending to some January 6 defendants, including those convicted of violence. The proposal has drawn bipartisan criticism over concerns that it could benefit people involved in the Capitol attack.

Hundreds of riot defendants are now seeking multi-million-dollar payouts, as critics describe the program as a “slush fund” that could reward Trump allies and those charged in the assault.

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has not ruled out payments to individuals who attacked police officers, while two officers injured during the riot have already filed lawsuits challenging the fund.

Trump told reporters Wednesday that people he described as victims of “weaponization” under the Obama and Biden administrations — referring to allies investigated in connection with his 2016 and 2020 campaigns and January 6, were “destroyed,” saying they went to jail, had their families ruined, and some “committed suicide.”

“We’re reimbursing those people for their legal fees and for their costs, and for anybody involved,” he said. “It was the most violent thing I’ve ever seen in politics.”

George Russell savoured a “special feeling” after pulling a pole lap out on his final run to land a double blow on title rival Kimi Antonelli at the Canadian Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old continued Mercedes’ run of claiming pole at every race this season and will line up at the front of the grid for the third time in a row in Montreal.

Mercedes had looked a little off the pace for much of the session but, at the death, Antonelli moved to the top of the standings only to be usurped on his final attempt by Russell.

The pair had earlier banged wheels during the sprint race as Antonelli accused Russell of pushing him off the track.

The British driver whooped in delight over the radio, before later saying: “It is such a special feeling.

“It (the lap) was incredibly strong, all the sweeter because it was so challenging before then.

“I never had it hooked up until that last lap in Q3. The times when you are fighting for it, are never up there and it comes together on that final lap to be the one is the best feeling in the world.”

Antonelli’s move around the outside of turn six during the sprint sparked the first flashpoint of the season between the title-chasing pair.

He raged over the radio after taking to the grass, with team principal Toto Wolff intervening to tell the 19-year-old to “stop the radio moaning”.

open image in gallery George Russell claimed a third successive pole in Montreal (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Antonelli was still angry after the sprint, where he lost out on second to Lando Norris after running across the grass again mid-fury, but Mercedes said they had debriefed before qualifying.

The Italian said: “We had a discussion, we clarified and now it is all good. We reviewed, we had a chat with Toto and all good.”

Russell echoed that view, saying: “We are not going to wave anybody by, whether it is a competitor or a team-mate.

“It is all good now, we know what we need to do and how we are going to race each other.

“We are team-mates, we have a good bond and it was obvious we needed to have a chat.

“We are both professionals and it was no real big deal afterwards. Nothing is personal when it is on track, it is history and now we look forward.

“We are racers, we are fighters, we wear our heart on our sleeve.

“Everything we think and feel is broadcast to the world. We are here to fight.”

The FIA has declared a rain hazard for Sunday’s race, with over a 40 per cent chance of wet weather.

open image in gallery A rain hazard has been declared for Sunday’s race (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

The vast majority of drivers have not driven this generation of cars, which are heavily electrified and have less grip and downforce than the previous era – with getting heat into the tyres a major factor.

There is a lot of caution about how they might perform.

Norris said: “We have never driven in the rain. I don’t think anyone knows how difficult it is going to be to drive these cars around here in the wet.

“It is our job at the end of the day, but I think it could be an insanely tricky race.”

Donald Trump announced Saturday that a major peace agreement with Iran is near finalization, following a high-level conference call from the Oval Office with key regional leaders.

Writing on Truth Social, the U.S. president stated that a Memorandum of Understanding has been “largely negotiated,” subject to final details being settled between the U.S., the Islamic Republic of Iran, and a broad coalition of Middle Eastern and South Asian nations.

The breakthrough comes after a series of calls involving the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, Turkey and Pakistan's military chief.

Trump also confirmed he held a separate, concurrent call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding the framework, which he described as having gone “very well.”

A central element of the emerging deal is the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical channel for global oil supplies that the conflict has heavily disrupted.

The announcement comes hours after President Donald Trump warned he was prepared to ‘blow them to a thousand hells’ if Tehran rejected American terms ( Reuters )

The White House stated that the final aspects of the agreement are currently being discussed by negotiators and a formal announcement is expected shortly.

The sudden announcement follows a period of heavy escalation and direct military threats.

Hours before his Truth Social post, Trump issued an ultimatum warning that he would return to open warfare if Tehran rejected American terms, Axios reported.

“Either we reach a good deal or I'll blow them to a thousand hells,” Trump said.

He added that he would review the latest draft agreement with senior advisers — including Vice President JD Vance, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner — on Saturday before making a final decision by Sunday on whether to resume military operations.

Trump stated he would only sign a deal where the U.S. gets “everything we want,” including provisions ensuring Iran's enriched uranium is “satisfactorily handled.”

The threat showed the fragile nature of the current ceasefire, which has paused the Iran war since April 8.

Negotiations had previously stalled over control of the shipping lane. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei had said that neighboring coastal states — rather than the U.S. — should dictate security protocols for the Strait.

Before the president's sudden Oval Office calls, peace talks had appeared to be failing. This prompted the Pentagon to prepare for an immediate escalation, with U.S. military and intelligence officials cancelling their Memorial Day weekend plans in anticipation of potential airstrikes if the talks collapsed.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking during a visit to New Delhi, confirmed that progress was being made by negotiators behind the scenes. Under the proposed framework, the U.S. and Iran would agree to halt military action and enter 30 days of formal negotiations aimed at securing a broader, permanent agreement.

News.title: Elderly California couple found dead in suspected murder-suicide were targeted by scammer posing as actor Tom Selleck
News.content:

An elderly couple found dead inside their California home in what investigators believe was a murder-suicide had been targeted as part of a scam, according to a longtime friend who says the woman believed she was communicating with actor Tom Selleck.

Donald Whitaker, 80, and his wife, Karen Whitaker, 79, were found dead on May 15 during a welfare check at their home in Bermuda Dunes, the Riverside County Sheriff’s Office said. Both had suffered traumatic injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene.

Investigators said Thursday that Karen Whitaker had been the victim of financial elder abuse, but stressed there is no evidence the scammer or scammers were directly involved in the deaths.

Joy Miedecke, 81, who said she had known the couple for more than a decade through the East Valley Republican Women Patriots club, said a neighbor requested a welfare check after Karen failed to show up for a regular Friday morning card game.

Miedecke told NBC News that the alleged scam began about a year ago after Karen posted on Facebook about a high school friend who had died. Soon afterward, someone contacted her claiming to be actor Tom Selleck.

open image in gallery Donald Whitaker, 80, and his wife, Karen Whitaker, 79, were found dead on May 15 ( Facebook/NBC Palm Springs )

“Somebody got a hold of her on Facebook and said they were Tom Selleck, and that they had dated this girl years ago,” Miedecke said Friday.

Believing the person was genuine, Karen shared her phone number and began texting with the alleged scammer, Miedecke said. Over time, the person gained Karen’s trust and eventually began asking for money. Miedecke said the first request came in November, when Karen was told she could attend an event in the desert for $80.

“Then, the [scammer or scammers] said, ‘We’re going to come out to the desert and have an event, and Karen, you can be first on the list if you just send $80,’ ” Miedecke said.

The money was allegedly sent through gift cards, a tactic the Federal Trade Commission has warned is commonly used by scammers because it allows quick access to funds once card numbers are shared.

According to Miedecke, the requests escalated from there.

“He kept writing her and gaining her trust and becoming her friend,” she said. “And then he decided that he was going to have the event again and told her you can buy a whole table for all your friends, it’s $800. She immediately sent him $800. That was the beginning. Then he needed money for this, and that and the other, and it just kept growing.”

Friends repeatedly warned Karen she was being scammed, Miedecke said, but she refused to believe them. Miedecke contacted the Riverside County Sheriff’s Office, and deputies spoke with Karen and provided “lots of proof” that the messages were fraudulent. Authorities confirmed that a report of financial elder abuse had been filed before the couple’s deaths.

Miedecke said the messages eventually became “almost a little bit romantic,” prompting her to seek additional help through adult protective services.

“She thought it was really Tom Selleck,” Miedecke told PEOPLE. “Nobody could stop her.”

According to Miedecke, Donald Whitaker first learned the full extent of the situation when adult protective services workers visited the couple’s home in January. She said the couple’s adult children tried to stop the financial losses by closing accounts and cutting up Karen’s credit cards.

open image in gallery The couple, found dead at their Bermuda Dunes home, had been entangled in an alleged scam with someone posing as actor Tom Selleck, their longtime friend said ( Google Maps )

“They cut up all of her credit cards, they closed the accounts, but she still found ways to get money,” Miedecke said. “She started hiding everything, but she’d be texting all day and all night, it was continuous.”

Miedecke said she believes Karen may have been experiencing early-stage dementia. She also said Donald struggled emotionally and financially after learning about the scam.

“He had said a couple of times to friends that he didn’t know how to handle this and he couldn’t cope with it,” Miedecke said.

The day before the couple’s deaths, Miedecke said Karen had again asked friends for money, claiming Selleck’s manager needed financial help after his wife died.

“That was the last straw for Donald,” Miedecke told PEOPLE. “He was so embarrassed. He could not believe she would ask her friends to participate in this scam.”

Miedecke said she hopes sharing Karen’s story will warn others about online scams targeting vulnerable people.

“The ramifications of someone stealing all of your money when you’re not capable of earning more money in your lifetime – look at what it causes,” she said.

The Riverside County Sheriff’s Office said homicide investigators are continuing to investigate the case. Selleck has not been accused of any wrongdoing or involvement.
